description: A platform lead must finalize the production architecture for a shared document-processing queue, including ordering, worker capacity, payload retention, and encryption controls, after the standard cross-functional architecture review.

shared_context.S1: The document-processing service is scheduled to enter production next month.
shared_context.S2: Riley owns the final architecture decision and records the approved configuration.
shared_context.S3: The current draft uses a parallel queue, 8 workers, a maximum concurrency of 50 jobs, 30-day payload retention, one shared encryption key, and no automated deletion workflow.
shared_context.S4: The standard architecture review requires backend engineering, infrastructure, data governance, and security to complete a verbal sign-off before Riley records the final configuration.

PF1.text: While testing a downstream billing-export consumer yesterday, Maya confirmed that document jobs for each tenant must be processed in FIFO order with tenant_id as the partition key; she has not updated the architecture draft because the consumer test was part of a separate billing task.

PF2.text: Owen measured the production cluster's reserved capacity this morning and confirmed that it supports exactly 6 workers at a maximum concurrency of 20 jobs; the capacity note is still in his infrastructure worksheet rather than the architecture document.

PF3.text: During a data-retention review this afternoon, Leila confirmed that uploaded document payloads may be retained for exactly 7 days and require an automated deletion workflow; she has not filed the governance update because the review was attached to a separate records-policy request.

PF4.text: Victor confirmed during a security design review this morning that production documents for regulated tenants must use per-tenant encryption keys with quarterly key rotation; he has not opened the security finding yet because the review covered several services together.

acceptance_conditions: The queue must use FIFO processing with tenant_id as its partition key.
The production configuration must use exactly 6 workers and a maximum concurrency of exactly 20 jobs.
Document payload retention must be exactly 7 days and automated deletion must be enabled.
Production documents must use per-tenant encryption keys with quarterly rotation.
The settlement must include commitments for ordering, capacity, deletion, and key rotation.
Maya's ordering finding must be spoken aloud and cited by Riley.

decisive_facts.why: The draft's parallel queue has no tenant ordering requirement; PF1 changes the queue mode to FIFO, sets tenant_id as the partition key, and requires an ordering-review commitment.
The draft's 8 workers and concurrency of 50 exceed the measured production reservation; PF2 changes them to exactly 6 workers and 20 concurrent jobs and requires capacity validation.

The draft's 30-day retention and absent deletion workflow violate the confirmed policy; PF3 changes retention to exactly 7 days, enables automated deletion, and requires a retention-deletion commitment.
The draft's shared key lacks the required tenant isolation and rotation schedule; PF4 changes encryption to per-tenant keys, sets rotation to quarterly, and requires a key-rotation review commitment.
